| '''[[Glasgow-3181|John Glasgow]] was the father of Katherine Glasgow and a second child whose name is provisionally read as Androw (Andrew).''' Margaret, provisionally surnamed Cochrane, was John's widow. The record expressly calls the children his lawful bairns and later repeats that John was their father. == Record and dates ==

This is an Edinburgh Commissary Court '''testament dative and inventory''', not a will dictated by John. The clear marginal date is '''4 May 1577'''. The death clause reads '''March''', but its year has not been securely deciphered; 1577 is the court or index year and should not automatically be used as the year of death.<ref name="JohnTestament">National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/5, images 276–277, testament dative and inventory of Johne Glasgw; working transcription of the original manuscript. The published index is ''Commissariot of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments, 1514–1600'', [https://archive.org/details/commissariotreco16scot/page/n117/mode/2up?q=Glasgow p. 109], entry dated 4 May 1577.</ref>

The derivative testament index identifies John as being '''in Hirmenschelis'''. That is useful evidence for the record's identity, but the place-name in the manuscript remains unclear in the present working reading and should not be silently supplied inside the transcription.<ref name="Index">[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FWILLS%2F057444&tab=this Findmypast, Scotland, Will and Testament Index 1481–1807, record SCOT/WILLS/057444], John Glasgow in Hirmenschelis, 4 May 1577; derivative index entry.</ref>

The confirmation repeats Katherine and [Andrew?] as executors to John, ''thair father''. Their parentage therefore does not depend on surname, household proximity or appointment alone. A separate debt entry says that '''Katherin Glasgow, servant''', was owed wages. She may be the same Katherine as the daughter, but that entry does not say so.

== Working transcription ==

Abbreviations are expanded and punctuation supplied. '''[Name?]''' marks a tentative reading; '''[…]''' marks unresolved text.

=== Opening ===

: '''Johne Glasgw. Quarto Maij 1577.'''
:
: The testament dative & inventar of the gudis, geir, sowmes of money & dettis pertening to umquhile Johne Glasgw in [place unclear], the tyme of his deceis, quha deceissit in the moneth of Marche, the zeir of God Iᵐ Vᶜ [numerals unclear], faithfullie maid & gevin up be '''Margaret [Cochrane?], his relict''', in name & behalf of '''Katharine & [Androw?] Glasgwis''', [pronoun unclear] '''lauchfull barnis & executouris dativis decernit to thair said umquhile father''' be decreit of the commissaris of Edinburgh, as the samin decreit of the dait the [day unclear] day of [Apryle?], the zeir of God Iᵐ Vᶜ lxxvij zeiris, at lenth proportis.

=== Inventory ===

John's possessions included '''two cows at £5 each''', '''two two-year-old cattle at four merks each''', a mare, sheep of mixed ages, apparently '''ten bolls of oats''' in the barn and barnyard, '''two bolls of barley valued together at £5''', household utensils and furnishings, and his clothing. Some quantities, individual valuations and the total remain unresolved in the manuscript reading.

=== Debts due to and by the estate ===

The section headed ''Followis the dettis awand to the deid'' lists people who owed John money. Recoverable but variably secure names include Alexander Paterson, William [Flint?], William Douglas, John Wilson, John [Millar?], John Mathie, William [Weir?], Peter [Baillie?], James [Mathie?], and a person surnamed Murray. Grain, including a boll of oats, occurs in some entries. These are financial associates, not stated relatives.

The debts owed by John include the balance of rent to '''James [Stevinsoun?] of [place unclear]''', wages to '''Thomas [surname unclear], servant''', and wages to '''Katherin Glasgow, servant'''. The recorded outgoing debts total '''£6'''. The free estate was then divided into three parts, but the remaining figures have not been securely read.

=== Confirmation ===

The useful surviving wording includes:

: … the saidis '''Katharine & [Androw?] Glasgwis in executouris dativis to the said umquhile Johne Glasgw thair father''', with power to thame to intromet … satisfie and pay the dettis …

In modern English, Katherine and [Andrew?] Glasgow were confirmed as court-appointed administrators of their late father John's estate, with authority to take charge of it and pay its debts.

== Genealogical assessment ==

* '''Proved:''' John Glasgow was father of Katherine and the second child [Andrew?].
* '''Proved:''' Margaret was John's surviving wife.
* '''Not proved by this wording:''' Margaret was the children's mother.
* '''Possible only:''' the servant Katherine and John's daughter Katherine were one person.
* '''Unresolved:''' Margaret's surname, the second child's forename, the manuscript place-name and the exact year of John's death.

The record remains compatible with the index identification of John in Hirmenschelis and with [[Glasgow-3181]], but relationships formerly built from different readings of the widow and second child require reassessment rather than preservation as facts.
